operation_additions.name: RAKP Control
operation_additions.purpose: Gets or sets Supermicro's proprietary RAKP compatibility mode. When enabled, netipmid selects the SMC RAKP path and rejects standard RAKP; when disabled, standard IPMI 2.0 RAKP remains available.
operation_additions.safety_note: Setting this flag can terminate compatibility with ordinary IPMI 2.0 clients and deny subsequent standard remote IPMI access. It is a transport-mode switch, not evidence that CVE-2021-39296's underlying session-state defect was repaired.

request.length: Exactly 1 byte for get or 2 bytes for set
request.summary: Action 0 gets EnableSMCRAKP; action 1 sets it to boolean 0 or 1.

fields.name: enabled
fields.meaning: Required only for set; 0=standard RAKP, 1=Supermicro proprietary RAKP

response.length: Exactly 1 byte for get; 0 bytes for set
response.summary: Get returns the current boolean; set returns no data.

operation_additions.interface: Raw OEM NetFn 0x30 over authenticated IPMI
operation_additions.availability: Introduced in BMC 01.07.00.06; absent from the audited 01.01.06.07 provider.
operation_additions.completion_codes: 0x00 success; 0xC7 wrong request length; 0xCC unknown action; 0xFF D-Bus failure
operation_additions.live_text: Safe 01.07.00.06 run: get request 00 returned 00; matching D-Bus property read returned false.
operation_additions.evidence: OEMGetSetRAKPCtrlCmd at ELF 0x1482f4; xyz.openbmc_project.Settings /com/SMCI/SMCRAKP com.SMCI.Managers.Item.SMCRAKP.EnableSMCRAKP; netipmid reads the same property during RAKP1/2 session establishment.
operation_additions.confidence: High: exact registration, typed request/response ABI, handler body, persistence backend, consumer, and safe live get are independently evidenced.

operation_additions.name: I2C Master Write/Read
operation_additions.purpose: Performs a raw write, read, or combined write-then-read transaction against /dev/i2c-N. This is an OEM adaptation of IPMI's Master Write-Read concept using a literal Linux bus number.
operation_additions.safety_note: This Administrator primitive exposes arbitrary enabled BMC I2C buses without a handler-local bus or device allowlist. Writes can reconfigure devices; combined I2C_RDWR transfers can address devices claimed by kernel drivers.

request.summary: Selects a Linux I2C bus and 7-bit address, then supplies read count and optional write bytes.

fields.name: address_byte
fields.meaning: Values 0x01..0xfe; handler uses address_byte >> 1 and ignores the low bit

fields.name: write_data
fields.meaning: Optional bytes written before any requested read

response.summary: Returns only the requested read bytes; pure writes and no-op transfers return no data.

fields.name: read_data
fields.meaning: Raw bytes returned by the selected I2C device

operation_additions.interface: Raw OEM NetFn 0x32 over authenticated IPMI
operation_additions.availability: Introduced in BMC 01.07.00.06; absent from the audited 01.01.06.07 provider.
operation_additions.completion_codes: 0x00 success; 0xC7 fewer than three request bytes; 0xCC address byte 0x00 or 0xff; 0xFF open, ioctl, read, write, or short-transfer failure
operation_additions.live_text: Safe 01.07.00.06 run: a deliberately short request returned 0xC7, proving registration and decoder reachability without touching an I2C device.
operation_additions.evidence: I2CMasterWriteRead at ELF 0x1421ac; /dev/i2c-%u, I2C_SLAVE 0x703, and I2C_RDWR 0x707 callsites recovered from the handler; enabled buses and devices cross-checked against the firmware DTB.
operation_additions.confidence: High: exact registration, full handler control flow, Linux ioctl semantics, response construction, and safe short-request dispatch are independently evidenced.

operation_additions.name: Leakage Detection Control
operation_additions.purpose: Gets or sets liquid-leak response policy, power lock, or detector enable state through the leakage-manager and persistent settings objects.
operation_additions.safety_note: The setters can change forced-off or graceful-shutdown reaction policy, lock power behavior, or enable/disable all leak detectors. Do not probe setters on production liquid-cooled systems.

request.summary: Recovered semantics are operation 0=get or 1=set and item 1=power reaction, 2=power lock, 4=detector enable; the exact successful typed-decoder layout is not yet proven.

fields.name: value
fields.meaning: Set only: item 1 accepts 0=keep current state, 1=graceful shutdown, 2=force off; items 2 and 4 accept boolean 0 or 1

response.length: Statically 1 byte for get and 0 bytes for set; successful wire layout not live-confirmed
response.summary: Get returns the selected policy/boolean value; set returns no data.

fields.name: value
fields.meaning: Get only: selected policy or boolean state

operation_additions.availability: Introduced in BMC 01.07.00.06; 0x68 selectors 0x39 and 0xdb retain Add/Delete User and Report Debug Message respectively.
operation_additions.completion_codes: 0x00 success; 0xC7 typed request-length error; 0xCC invalid operation, item, or value; 0xD5 no leakage-manager object; 0xFF backend exception
operation_additions.live_text: Safe 01.07.00.06 run: selector-only and candidate get payloads returned 0xC7, confirming dispatch but disproving the initial wire-layout hypothesis; no setter was sent.
operation_additions.evidence: OEMLeakageDetectionControl at ELF 0x0f815c; selector tuple at constructor 0x6cc74-0x6cc94; settings objects /com/SMCI/LeakagePowerOption and /com/SMCI/LeakagePowerLock; SensorEnable on /com/supermicro/leakagemanager/*; leakage-manager persists /var/liquid_cooling_state.json.
operation_additions.confidence: High for selector ownership, operations, values, backends, and effects; Partial for the exact post-selector request ABI and successful response framing.

operation_additions.name: Enable NVSSVT
operation_additions.purpose: Persists a boolean compatibility flag consumed by bmcweb's SmartNIC sensor-collection path for NVIDIA System Software Validation Toolkit integration.
operation_additions.safety_note: Creates or overwrites a persistent configuration flag. It enables NVSSVT-oriented BMC web behavior; it does not itself launch the NVIDIA toolkit.

request.summary: Writes boolean 0 or 1 to the persistent NVSSVT flag.

operation_additions.availability: Introduced in BMC 01.07.00.06; selector 0x70:0x3a remains the existing Notify BMC Sensor Start stub.
operation_additions.completion_codes: 0x00 success; 0xC7 wrong request length; 0xCE value greater than 1; 0xFF flag-file open or write failure
operation_additions.live_text: No mutating request sent; the flag was absent on the live 01.07.00.06 guest before authentication became unavailable.
operation_additions.evidence: EnableNVSSVT at ELF 0x0a2c8c writes ASCII 0 or 1 to /var/configuration/enable-nvssvt.flag; bmcweb SHA-256 56a3489ac4abcba71b99118ae0643f691abb8f0cb7e60a8085ba7bb6af5c6926 is the only other firmware binary referencing that path, in its SmartNIC sensor collection implementation.
operation_additions.confidence: High: exact selector, request/response ABI, validation, file side effect, and sole firmware consumer are independently evidenced.
